inputs.target: response points on the opponent's turn with my life <= 3 and turn >= 4; end-of-turn: last 1-2 MAIN points of my turn with my life <= 3 and turn >= 4

cost.wall: about 3.5 h for 300 games on 4 workers (run was restarted twice by worker restarts; resumes by seed)

command: python tests/scripts/defense_audit.py run --games 300 --workers 4 && python tests/scripts/defense_audit.py verify --workers 4 && python tests/scripts/defense_audit.py summarize

gates.make_test: green on the final tree (2026-10-22 23:5x UTC): cargo test 601 passed / 1 ignored; pytest 855 passed, 13 skipped

notes: Headline: 3/4 of the verified otsu misses (21/28) are blind replays of a defense-box commit (decide kind 'commit', no tree) planned at the preceding blocker/counter window; a fresh decide without the carried commit picks a safe response in all 21. 18 of them are 'PASS at life 0 with a holding counter in hand' = immediate loss.

Likely mechanism (code reading, unverified): rust/opcg_engine/src/search/decide.rs move_sig reads payload.uuid only; battle moves carry the card in card_uuid, so a committed SELECT_COUNTER step has signature [SELECT_COUNTER, null, ...] and find_move replays the FIRST legal counter (possibly a smaller one), then the committed PASS goes through. Not fixed here (read-only WP). Proposed follow-up: include card_uuid in move_sig, or re-decide at battle windows instead of trusting the commit; re-audit the same 300 games and check that the 21 points disappear.

Target filter mirrors §7.13 for cost: my life <= 3 and turn >= 4 (the spec did not fix the filter; chosen for comparability). Points on my own turn where I answer the opponent's effect are not included (only the opponent's turn).

Otsu redeal is from the defender's view: the attacker's hand + deck + face-down life are redealt (true + offense-strong + offense-weak + 4 random). The defender's own deck/life are left as is (same as §7.13). Deals are rebuilt via Game.from_hidden, so points with an interaction stack or pending triggers are skipped for otsu (recorded as skip).

Solver approximations are those of lethal_audit.py (attacker: leader attacks only, DON attach only onto the attacking unit; dialogs: one target at a time). They under-count the attacker, i.e. over-count 'safe' responses; the verify pass re-judges every miss with the full solver (character attacks + free DON) at 30 s and removed 7 (ko) / 4 (otsu) as unknown-or-not-safe. The remaining 'unknown' are not confirmed misses.

End-of-turn audit: alternatives that win the game outright under default resolution (opponent passes) are the §7.13 own-lethal question and are excluded (9 of 136 threat turns had one). The default resolution assumes the opponent does not counter my alternative attack, so the 3 raw / 1 verified end misses are optimistic. unknown_actual is 61% at 10 s (the opponent's turn head has many options), so the threat-turn count is a lower bound.

The turn-head judge (end audit) was given its own 10 s cap (--sec-end) instead of the 5 s of §7.13 because the pilot showed 52% unknown at 5 s; its transposition table is shared with the same turn's response points so the cost is mostly recovered.

Intermediate pushes (partial jsonl) carried only data plus the tool; make test was run once on the tool at the first push (green: cargo 601 passed, pytest 855 passed / 13 skipped) and once more on the final tree before the final push (see gates).

The container's worker was restarted twice during the run (the python workers died with it); the run resumes by seed and was relaunched with setsid. Wall time about 3.5 h. No games were reduced (300/300).
pytest-xdist, fastapi, httpx and maturin were pip-installed in this container to build the wheel and run make test.
